template_z returns NaN for an infinite lam, or for n_cells = NaN. On lam = inf, the far-tail fallback computes (K-1) log(inf) - inf, which is NaN. Python's min(nan, 0.0) keeps the NaN (the first argument wins), and _gauss_z(nan) is NaN. A NaN Z compares False against any threshold, so such a peak is silently dropped rather than reported as overwhelming.
em_pins.hpp TEMPLATE_Z rows {INF_, 33, 1.0} -> NaN and {40, 33, NAN_} -> NaN; sstvae/qrss/em.py:419-427
_gauss_z(-inf) returns NaN instead of +inf: the Mills iteration computes sqrt(inf), then inf - 2 log(inf * sqrt(2 pi)), which is NaN.

template_z with n_chunks <= 0 does not refuse cleanly. gamma.logsf returns NaN for a <= 0, which sends the call to the fallback, and math.lgamma(0 or -2) raises a bare ValueError 'math domain error'. With lam <= 0 in the fallback, math.log raises the same.
em_pins.hpp TEMPLATE_Z rows (40, 0, 1), (40, -2, 1), (0, 0, 1) -> 'math domain error'; em.py:421-425

lmmse_latents keeps a NaN weight (np.maximum propagates NaN), so a single NaN W poisons its whole precoder block's v through block_mean. This is unreachable through Store.merge, which refuses non-finite input, but a hand-made (S, W) passed to prior_from carries it.
inferred from code: em.py:110-130; pinned case k=4 (w[2] = NaN) in gen_em_pins.prior_case

CPython's math.lgamma is its own Lanczos approximation (Modules/mathmodule.c m_lgamma), not the C library's lgamma, and the two differ in the last place for roughly half of all arguments. Porting it as math::py_lgamma made template_z's far-tail fallback bit-exact.
scratch sweep: 0 mismatches against math.lgamma over about 70k arguments after the port; LGAMMA_DIGEST in em_pins.hpp

scipy 1.18.1 has no gamma._logsf of its own: rv_continuous._logsf applies apply_where(x > gammaincinv(a, 0.5), log(gammaincc), log1p(-gammainc)), and numpy's SIMD log/log1p differ from libm by an ulp at some points. So gamma.logsf cannot be bit-exact without reimplementing numpy's SIMD log.
11 of 40060 points not bitwise, worst 2.05e-16 rel; 110-value pinned table worst 2.14e-16
norm.isf(q) is -ndtri(q)*1.0+0.0, so isf(0.5) is +0.0, not -0.0. scipy's cephes ndtri calls only libm's log and sqrt, so it ports bit for bit.
test_special.cpp norm_isf(0.5) signbit check; NDTRI_DIGEST over 736 values

scipy 1.18.1's gamma.logsf is not plain log(sf): rv_continuous._logsf splits at the median (x > gammaincinv(a, 0.5) -> log(gammaincc), else log1p(-gammainc)). The search is FFT-bound and both sides use pocketfft, so the gain is ~2.2-3.3x, not 10x. Per search_chan call (K=128, 19 bins): products 27 ms -> AVX2 clone, |C|^2 28 ms -> AVX2 branch-free hypot (bit-identical, NaN/inf lanes checked), IFFTs 53 ms per-row -> 36 ms batched 32 rows per pocketfft call (memcmp-identical); total 111 -> 65 ms vs numpy 175 ms. The remaining levers are not bit-exact or need build changes: wider-SIMD pocketfft needs a separate -mavx2 TU (CMake), threads across the 19 bins would give ~4x but no core QRSS code is threaded yet.

pocketfft's multi-row c2c (rows in SIMD lanes) gives exactly the bits of one-row-at-a-time exec, so batching is free for parity; numpy's np.abs on complex128 is a SIMD hypot (larger*sqrt(fma(r,r,1)) with explicit inf/NaN selection) whose branch-free AVX2 form reproduces np::abs lane for lane.
bench_batch: 'identical 1'; bench_abs: 'identical 1, value diffs 0' including inf/NaN/zero inputs

A ctest that needs a capture with a real detection can be built without committed sample data: the formula store's own template (prior_from + make_classes + chunk_template with chunk 1) planted at a chosen lag/step/bin into splitmix noise, phases from libm cos/sin on an exactly-reduced turn, then rounded to float32. C++ and Python then agree to ~2e-16 on Z, so 1e-9 pins have six orders of margin; one mutation of the drift derotation fails 11 checks.

receive_template on SHORT with a CW-known member is the only place this lane misses 1e-6. track.refine_timing is a finite-difference Newton with h = 0.3 samples, and it turns last-ulp differences in its input into about 3e-5 of the ppm. template_search's output is bit-identical going in, so this is the track lane's sensitivity, not an em_search error. A pass found at the detection gate inherits it.

Fragile spot in the reference: template_search on a 250 Hz capture calls chan.noise_floor() per candidate, and the floor raises ZeroDivisionError (0 samples) or ValueError (1 sample) on a capture too short for it. Whether a search refuses therefore depends on whether any candidate reaches the capture. The port now copies this ordering instead of hiding it. Python is unchanged.

em_refine's progress contract is not 'total never falls': when EM converges early its last call is (done, done, 'converged after round r'), lowering total to done. em_api.hpp first documented it wrong and test_em_api's monotonicity check caught it on the first run; the header and the check now state the exception, which is what a progress bar needs (close the bar at done, not at the planned total).
first test_em_api run: 'FAIL refine converging: total never falls at call 3'; native/core/qrss/em_refine.hpp:194-202

A Python call that numbers rounds from 1 on every invocation (em_refine: for r in range(1, rounds+1), em_round = r) means a second `--em 1` leaves every member at 'EM round 1' again, not 2 -- the member's em_round is the round of its last re-receive within one call, not a cumulative count. My reverse test assumed cumulative and failed; worth knowing for an app that shows 'EM round' as progress across button presses.

Not a bug but a hazard: qrss_decode.py --em N with N huge iterates range(1, N+1) and em_refine's history loop would run up to N rounds if every round kept gaining >= tol_db; there is no cap. Bounded in practice by convergence (tol 0.05 dB).

In the chain test, choosing the weak pass's frame matters for honesty: a TINY pass in a recording listened with --frame short is 'missed' trivially. Checking the listener's passes/ directory (one .npz) is what makes 'the live receiver missed it, the template search found it' a tested claim.

Accumulator.uids returns members' uids unchecked and em_refine's round loop re-receives and update_pass()es members in order, so a damaged member part-way down the list leaves the store half-refined when the ValueError from _pass_path finally fires (known_header only protects the case where it reaches the bad member first). Not wrong per se, but em_refine has no all-or-nothing guarantee on a damaged accumulator.
